models.name: discussionboard_categories
models.description: Discussion board categories - Implements categorization as specified in the requirements analysis section regarding navigability, content organization, and moderation targeting. This model supports organized user experience and functional requirements for thread placement, filtering, and role-based content management. Maintains 3NF by keeping category metadata atomic, without duplicating section or configuration data. For example, a member starts a thread under the 'Economics' category, which is mapped here for retrieval. Key relationships: references to discussionboard_sections (for section grouping) and possible linkage to threads (managed in another component). Special behaviors: categories can be disabled or reordered without affecting thread data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each category, supporting distributed system architecture and audit trailing.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_section_id
foreignFields.description: Parent section's {@link discussionboard_sections.id} - Implements hierarchical grouping as per business requirements, enabling categories to be nested within sections for enhanced organization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name - Implements the display and search requirement for category labeling. Ensures normalization by isolating the label as atomic data. For example, 'Politics', 'Economics', 'International' etc.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Category description - Provides contextual information to users and moderators. Maintains normalization by keeping explanations independent of other data. For instance, 'High-level discussions of macroeconomic issues.'

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Category display order - Controls sequence in UI navigation and listings. Maintains 3NF as it's not derived or duplicated from any other data. For example, '1' = top position on board.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Is category enabled - Implements business rule for soft-hiding or disabling a category without deleting its record. Used in admin flows to turn categories on/off. For example, admins can disable a category temporarily during moderation.

models.name: discussionboard_sections
models.description: Discussion board sections - Implements section-level grouping as per requirements covering board segmentation, navigation, and high-level access control. This entity solves the business need for upper-level organization beneath which categories (and subsequently threads) are grouped, supporting both frontend navigation and backend moderation targeting. Fully 3NF: atomic section label, description, and configuration linkage. For example, a section named 'Global Politics' groups multiple categories. Key relationships: can be referenced by categories and linked to board-wide configuration. Special behaviors: sections can be archived, reordered, or locked for content submission by toggling their enabled state.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each section, supporting scalable, distributed storage and system traceability.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Configuration link {@link discussionboard_configurations.id} - Associates the section with platform configuration for access control or behavior settings as per business policy.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section name - Implements navigation and search requirements for board-level organization. Normalized as atomic data. For example, 'Domestic Affairs', 'International Relations'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Section description - Context for users about the topical intent or rules. Fully normalized; avoids data redundancy. For instance, 'Contains threads related to domestic economic policy.'

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Section display order - Determines appearance in navigation and configuration panels. For example, order '0' = top section. 3NF: not dependent on non-key fields.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Is section enabled - Controls visibility and posting capability for the section. Provides admin tools for platform segmentation as required by business rules.

models.name: discussionboard_configurations
models.description: Discussion board configurations - Implements board-wide or section-specific settings, as required by platform policy and business rules for extensibility, permissions, and behavior customization. This model addresses operational flexibility: toggling feature flags, adjusting settings without schema changes, and supporting future platform growth. Maintains strict normalization: each configuration record atomic. For example, holding JSON settings for poll behaviors, default moderation options, or feature enablement. Key relationships: referenced by discussionboard_sections and possibly others in the future. Special behaviors: changes are audit-logged elsewhere; configurations are never deleted outright—only updated or replaced.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration, supporting distributed storage and reliable referencing by other entities.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Configuration name/key - Used for identification in admin tools and code. Normalized primary config label. Example: 'default_section_policy', 'poll_settings'.

plainFields.name: settings_json
plainFields.description: Serialized configuration JSON - Stores all behavioral settings as a JSON string. Normalized: each config in its own row. For example, '{"allow_polls": true, "max_poll_options": 10}'

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable descriptive text about the configuration's purpose. Maintains normalization. For instance, 'Settings controlling default behaviors for domestic threads.'

models.name: discussionboard_admins
models.description:
Admin Role Model - This implements the administrative user role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents site administrators who have full access for platform management, policy enforcement, user control, and official dispute handling. Maintains 3NF normalization by only holding role-specific identity, inheriting account details via shared foreign key references in actual system (e.g., via member or user account tables in other domains). For example, admins may be mapped to existing accounts for login. 

Key relationships: Not directly referencing other components to avoid duplication, but will use external user/member tables for ID in full implementation. 
Special behaviors: Only users elevated to this table have admin permissions; removal here revokes all admin rights.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique admin role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Implements the auditability requirement. Records when the admin privilege was granted. Ensures temporal traceability for permission changes, supporting snapshot patterns by explicitly separating the assignment history. For example, when new admins are added, this field logs the event.

models.name: discussionboard_moderators
models.description:
Moderator Role Model - This implements the moderator role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents users with moderation powers: content review, temporary suspensions, and community management, without full admin rights. 3NF compliance is achieved by separating moderator role assignments from general user/member identity, with actual references made to external user/member accounts for linkage. 

Key relationships: In a full system, would reference members/users for role mapping. 
Special behaviors: Inclusion grants moderation rights; records are auditable for community trust and escalation protocols.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique moderator role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Tracks when the moderator privilege was activated. Supports audit trails and historical analysis of role distribution and trust elevation. For example, elevated by senior admins or via governance process.

models.name: discussionboard_members
models.description:
Member Role Model - Implements core registered user account role as specified in '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents all authenticated users authorized to create content, interact, and participate in member-only features. Complies with 3NF by storing only role/enrollment information; user profile, security, and credentials exist in separate tables/domains. For example, email/username/password managed elsewhere but ID assigned here upon registration completion.

Key relationships: Mapped to outer user or authentication entity in wider system. 
Special behaviors: Granting/removing a row in this table assigns permission to create threads, participate in polls, etc.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique member role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Logged at registration or membership upgrade. Used for eligibility/rule tracking and supports audit trails. For example, new signups receive this timestamp.

models.name: discussionboard_guests
models.description:
Guest Role Model - Implements the guest browsing entity from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents unauthenticated and optionally semi-tracked users who may browse public content but not post/interact. Maintains 3NF as a distinct normalized table to assign and trace guest viewing sessions, apply access controls, and support future conversion (upgrade to member). For example, may store guest session or visitor tokens mapped to analytics.

Key relationships: May relate to external analytics/logs for guest tracking in broader system. 
Special behaviors: Deleting a guest here does not affect any member/admin records, ensuring normalization between roles.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique guest identifier, e.g., guest session or pseudonymous token.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Guest session/browsing assignment timestamp - Set when a guest session is first tracked or created. Used for analysis, conversion tracking to members, and policy enforcement (e.g., access window).

models.name: discussionboard_auth_sessions
models.description:
Authentication Session Model - Implements the authentication and session tracking requirement from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md' and ties policies in '05_discussionboard_business_rules_and_policies.md' (account locking, session expiry, etc.). 

Tracks active user/member sessions for login management, enforcing security policies, session timeouts, and role mapping. Complies with 3NF by separating session management from user identity, allowing independent lifecycle. For example, on login, a new row is created; on logout or expiry, row is ended.

Key relationships: Would reference user/member/role tables for session ownership in a full system.
Special behaviors: Supports device/session concurrency policies, auditing of all critical actions (policy: audit trail for edits, deletions, moderation decisions).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique session identifier.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Role type associated with the session. Implements session role typing for permission checks (e.g., 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', 'guest'). Ensures normalization by separating session against role tables. For example: 'member' session tracks a logged in member, 'guest' for unauthenticated visitor.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Associated actor id (admin/member/moderator/guest). Implements role linking for session ownership. Ensures normalization so that user/role are tracked externally, this is a foreign key reference in broader system. For example, points to the 'id' of the corresponding role table depending on actor_type.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: Session start timestamp. Implements session record creation for login audit trails. For example, set when user completes login.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp - Used to implement session expiry, security policy on inactivity, or explicit logout. For example, calculated by security policy or upon logout event.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last activity on this session. Implements last-used tracking for security checks (token expiration, forced logout). For example, updated on each page load or action.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Time at which session was revoked, if applicable. Implements security and forced logout. For example, set if session is invalidated by admin or system.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address recorded when session was initiated. Provides security auditing for login source and supports fraud monitoring. For example, '192.168.1.1'.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string recorded on session establishment. Implements browser/device tracking policy for audit and security. For example, 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10...)'.

models.name: discussionboard_threads
models.description:
Thread Root Entity - This implements the 'thread management and creation' requirement from the features and user journeys documentation. Each instance represents an individual discussion thread (topic) started by a member, with links to category/section and root post. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating main thread data (title, status, author/member, section/category) from posts, histories, and related engagement. For example, a new thread '2025 Elections Discussion' would have one record here and many related post/comment records elsewhere. 
Key relationships: Links to author member, category, and root post via foreign keys. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion (archived flag), per-thread lock/pin status for moderation/admins.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique thread identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Thread author's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Refers to the member who created the thread.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_category_id
foreignFields.description: Thread's assigned {@link discussionboard_categories.id}. Refers to the topic/category under which this thread is created.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Thread title - Implements the required summary/title as per requirements document. Atomic, and always present. For example: '2025 Economic Outlook'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Thread status - Active, archived, locked. Implements moderation control requirement. For example: 'active', 'locked', 'archived'.

plainFields.name: is_pinned
plainFields.description: Pinned flag - Whether this thread is pinned at the top. Implements thread management feature for moderators/admins. true if pinned by moderation.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: Locked flag - Whether this thread is locked. Implements moderation tool for controlling participation. true if thread no longer accepts replies.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: Soft delete/archive flag. If true, thread is hidden from public but data is retained for admins/audit. Implements audit/compliance rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Thread creation timestamp. For audit/logging as per business rules.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Thread last updated timestamp. Updated on edits or moderation events. Required for audit trail and UX.

models.name: discussionboard_posts
models.description: Thread Post Entity - Implements the 'thread and comment posting', 'reply', and 'content moderation/reporting' features. Each represents an individual post or comment in a thread, with parent-child relation for comments (nested structure). Maintains 3NF compliance by keeping each post atomic and referring to its thread, author, and parent. For example, a threaded reply is a record here with a parent post. Key relationships: thread linkage, post author (member), optional parent for comments. Special behaviors: supports nested replies, soft deletion.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique post identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced thread's {@link discussionboard_threads.id}. Indicates which thread this post belongs to.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Author member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Refers to the member who wrote this post or comment.

foreignFields.name: parent_post_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent {@link discussionboard_posts.id} (for replies/comments). Null for root posts; non-null for comments/replies to other posts.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Post content body. Implements textual content storage. Fully normalized. For example: 'I think the economic forecast is optimistic.'

plainFields.name: is_edited
plainFields.description: Edit flag. True if post has been edited after initial creation. Implements edit tracking policy.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag. True if post is hidden from general users, retained for moderation/audit. Implements compliance and moderation rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of post creation. For chronology, moderation review, and user display.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update. Reflects edit or moderation action.

models.name: discussionboard_post_histories
models.description: Post History Snapshot Entity - Implements post edit/version control requirement. Each record is a snapshot of a post's content and metadata before or after an edit/action, maintaining a complete audit trail. Ensures 3NF by storing versions separately. For example, if a post is edited three times, there are three snapshot entries linked to the post. Key relationships: belongs to post, links to member who performed the edit/action. Special rules: records must not be deletable by regular users, only by admin/audit purge.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique snapshot record identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Indicates which post this snapshot is for.

foreignFields.name: edit_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who performed the edit/action. For tracking responsible user.

plainFields.name: old_body
plainFields.description: Prior post body (before edit/action). Implements versioned content requirement. Null if post was created (not edited yet).

plainFields.name: new_body
plainFields.description: Edited (new) post body. Required for post change logs. Null if snapshot is for deletion (not rewording).

plainFields.name: edit_type
plainFields.description: Type of edit/action (e.g., 'edit', 'delete', 'restore'). For audit and moderation policy linkage. For example: 'edit', 'delete'.

plainFields.name: edit_reason
plainFields.description: Reason/comment for the edit, as recorded by the member or moderator. For moderation transparency, compliance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this history/snapshot record was created. Fully normalized.

models.name: discussionboard_post_edit_logs
models.description: Post Edit Log Entity - Implements granular audit-purposed logging for all post edits, satisfying compliance and traceability requirements beyond typical edit history. Each entry records who, when, and what change occurred, for every modification to any post. Maintains 3NF as every field relates directly to the primary key. For example, if a user performs three edits, all are logged here for admins/audits. Key relationships: links to post, edit-performing member.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique edit log record identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Edited post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}.

foreignFields.name: edit_member_id
foreignFields.description: Editing member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}.

plainFields.name: change_summary
plainFields.description: Brief summary of the edit. For quick audit purposes. Example: 'Fixed typo', 'Added reference'.

plainFields.name: change_details
plainFields.description: Detailed information about the change (could be JSON or text). For investigation and compliance. Example: '{"from":"draft version","to":"final version"}'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Edit timestamp. For chronology.

models.name: discussionboard_thread_archives
models.description: Thread Archive Entity - Implements thread archival/inactivation feature (from user cases/policies) whereby entire threads are hidden from public view on closure or due to compliance policy. This normalized entity stores archive records with references to thread, member (initiator), and reason. Example: a thread archived due to policy contains record here. Key relationships: links to thread, admin/mod who performed archival. Special behavior: archival should not delete thread/posts. Maintains 3NF.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique archive record identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Thread's {@link discussionboard_threads.id} being archived.

foreignFields.name: archived_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member (admin/moderator) {@link discussionboard_members.id} who performed the archival.

plainFields.name: archive_reason
plainFields.description: Reason/archive comment per moderation/audit policy implementation. Example: 'Thread closed for being off-topic.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Archival timestamp.

models.name: discussionboard_content_reports
models.description:
Content Report Entity - This implements the requirement for capturing and tracking user-reported content as defined in 'Business Rules and Policies' and across 'Features and Functional Specifications'.

This model records when a member or guest files a report on a post, comment, or thread for policy violations, harassment, or inappropriate content. It maintains normalized structure (3NF) by capturing report details and referencing the post/content in violation, along with the reporting user and reason. For example, when a member reports a post they believe is a violation, a new row is created here and linked to the moderation review process.

Key relationships: References reporter (member or guest by user_id/actor_id) and the offending content (from the threads/posts tables in the ThreadsPosts component).
Special behaviors: Maintains audit trail; supports escalation workflow and status updates.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each content report entry.

foreignFields.name: reported_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id} reported for violation or moderation. May also be used to reference a comment if required.

foreignFields.name: reporter_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}, if the reporter is a registered member.

foreignFields.name: reporter_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Reporting guest's {@link discussionboard_guests.id}, if the report was filed by a guest user (optional).

plainFields.name: report_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for content report - Implements requirement to capture user's motivation for reporting content. Ensures normalization by storing only reason text; examples include 'spam', 'abuse', 'off-topic', etc. Required for moderation triage and analytics.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Moderation status of the report - Implements status tracking for the moderation queue. Allowed values are 'pending', 'in_review', 'action_taken', 'dismissed', reflecting different workflow states. Ensures normalization by storing only the status token. For example, 'pending' is assigned on creation.

plainFields.name: reported_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the content was reported - Implements audit trail requirement and ensures detailed moderation history. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: moderator_note
plainFields.description: Moderator's note on review outcome - Allows documenting justification for resolution or further actions. Nullable; present after moderator review.

models.name: discussionboard_moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation Action Entity - Implements requirement for logging all actions taken by moderators or admins in response to reports, violations, or escalations as described in 'Features and Functional Specifications' and 'Business Rules and Policies'.

This model records every action taken during moderation (warning issued, thread locked, post deleted, user suspended, etc.), who performed it, and on which content or user. Maintains 3NF by linking actions to actors (moderator/admin), target content or users, and report IDs if applicable. E.g., When a moderator deletes a post for policy violation, this logs the event with details.

Key relationships: Relates to moderation actor, affected user (optional), and reported content. Also links to the report if action was a result of a report.
Special behaviors: Immutable audit log for compliance and appeals.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each moderation action.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Actor's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who performed the action. Required for accountability.

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: Related report's {@link discussionboard_content_reports.id}, if this action is linked to a content report. Nullable, as some actions may be proactive.

foreignFields.name: affected_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target content's {@link discussionboard_posts.id} affected by this action. Nullable, as some actions are user-account-related, not specific content.

foreignFields.name: affected_member_id
foreignFields.description: Affected member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}, if the action concerns a user account. For example, suspensions or warnings.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action taken - Implements audit trail and compliance requirements. Examples: 'warned', 'deleted_post', 'suspended_user', 'locked_thread', 'archived_thread'. Only atomic state; details are in the description. Keeps the table normalized. For example, 'warned' or 'deleted_post'.

plainFields.name: action_description
plainFields.description: Detailed description for the action - Implements need for justification and appeals. Ensures normalization by keeping only description in text. E.g., 'Post contained prohibited content per rule X.'

plainFields.name: action_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the moderation action - Implements audit trail and sequencing of moderation events.

models.name: discussionboard_warning_logs
models.description:
Warning Log Entity - Implements the requirement for tracking all warnings issued to members, as per acceptance criteria in User Roles, Functional Specifications, and Business Rules.

Each warning issued by a moderator/admin to a member is logged here, maintaining normalized structure by linking to both the issuer and recipient, along with reason and timestamp. For example, when a moderator warns a member for minor misconduct, this captures the event.

Key relationships: Links warning to the moderator (actor) and warned member (recipient), referencing both by IDs.
Special behaviors: Used for history checks and appeals, supports escalation of repeated violations.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each warning log.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator/admin's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who issued the warning. Required for accountability.

foreignFields.name: warned_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who received the warning.

plainFields.name: warning_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the warning - Implements requirement for capturing justification. Maintains normalization (atomic text value). E.g., 'inappropriate language' or 'off-topic reply'.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the warning was issued. Ensures auditability and time-order analysis. Not nullable.

models.name: discussionboard_suspensions
models.description:
Suspension Log Entity - Implements the requirement for tracking temporary user suspensions for policy violations or moderation reasons. Referenced in User Roles & Authentication, Functional Specifications, and Business Rules.

This model logs suspension actions with start/end timestamps, reason, actor (moderator/admin), and target member. Fully normalized; does not pre-calculate any suspension history summary. For example, if a member is suspended for spamming, a row is created here with dates and cause.

Key relationships: Links moderator (actor) and suspended member (recipient).
Special behaviors: Supports enforcement of suspensions and review for appeals or admin audit.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each user suspension record.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator/admin's {@link discussionboard_moderators.id} who performed the suspension.

foreignFields.name: suspended_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who was suspended.

plainFields.name: suspension_reason
plainFields.description: Reason suspension was issued - Implements requirement for tracking policy violations or abuse. Maintains 3NF (atomic value only). E.g., 'spamming', 'multiple policy violations'.

plainFields.name: suspension_started_at
plainFields.description: When suspension began - For audit trails and auto-expiry systems. Maintains precise timeline for enforcement.

plainFields.name: suspension_ends_at
plainFields.description: Scheduled end time for suspension - For auto-lifting suspensions and appeals. Null if indefinite or until manual review.

models.name: discussionboard_bans
models.description:
Ban Log Entity - Implements requirement for permanent user bans, as mandated in User Roles, Policies, and Auditing documentation.

Each row represents a permanent ban issued to a member (or, rare, a guest) by an admin; records cause, actor, issue time, and optional notes. Maintains normalized structure: each ban is atomic and links to relevant actor and user entities. For example, if an admin bans a member for repeated malicious activity, a record is created here.

Key relationships: Connects banned user (usually a member) and banning admin. May also target guests in some edge cases.
Special behaviors: Used for enforcement, audit, and appeals; notifies affected users per requirements.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each ban record.

foreignFields.name: banned_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who has been permanently banned.

foreignFields.name: banned_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest's {@link discussionboard_guests.id} who has been permanently banned (rare; usually members).

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin's {@link discussionboard_admins.id} who performed the ban.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the permanent ban - Implements tracking and appeal justification. Maintains 3NF (atomic value). E.g., 'repeated malicious activity' or 'severe policy breach'.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Ban issue timestamp - For system notification and legal reference. Not nullable.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional admin notes for the ban - Used for details and audit trail. Nullable and not required for all bans.

models.name: discussionboard_post_reactions
models.description: Post reaction entity - Implements the 'User Interactions and Engagement' requirement from the specifications. Each record is a normalized log of a user's emoji or symbolic response to a post. Maintains 3NF by having a single atomic value per reaction, with unique constraints over (post, member, type). For example, a member may react with a 'heart' emoji to a post.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Target post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. The post that received the reaction. Normalized foreign key.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reacting member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. The user who gave the reaction. Normalized foreign key.

plainFields.name: reaction_type
plainFields.description: Type of reaction (e.g., emoji name or standard). Atomic value, e.g., 'thumbs_up', 'heart'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the reaction was created for audit and time queries.

models.name: discussionboard_post_likes
models.description: Post like entity - Implements binary 'like' from a member to a post. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic likes (one like per user per post). For example, if a member likes a post, that action appears only once in the table. Unique over (post, member).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Liked post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. References the liked post in a normalized manner.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Liking member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. The member who liked the post. Normalized foreign key.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the like was recorded.

models.name: discussionboard_polls
models.description: Poll metadata entity - Implements member-driven polls inside threads. Represents an atomic poll question, its configuration, and creator. Maintains 3NF by not storing any derived results. Each poll is linked to a parent thread and a creator. Example: a poll about preferred economic policy within a thread.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Thread's {@link discussionboard_threads.id}. References the discussion thread this poll is attached to.

foreignFields.name: created_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Creator member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Member who started the poll, as normalized foreign key.

plainFields.name: prompt
plainFields.description: Poll prompt shown to users. For example: 'Which policy is best?'

plainFields.name: allow_multiple_choices
plainFields.description: Allow voters to choose more than one option. True for multi-select polls.

plainFields.name: is_anonymous
plainFields.description: Indicates if the poll is anonymous. True means individual votes are hidden.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Poll expiration timestamp. Nullable if the poll never expires.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the poll was created.

models.name: discussionboard_poll_votes
models.description: Poll voting entity - Each record shows a member's atomic vote for a poll option. Enforces strict 3NF with unique over (poll, member, option) for multi-choice, or per poll in single-choice situation. Used for direct normalization of poll voting results. Example: If a user votes Option A on Poll 1, that's one row.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_poll_id
foreignFields.description: Owns to poll {@link discussionboard_polls.id}. The poll this vote is for.

foreignFields.name: voting_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. The voter who cast this ballot.

plainFields.name: selected_option
plainFields.description: User-selected value (poll option label or id if normalized elsewhere).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this vote was cast.

models.name: discussionboard_mentions
models.description: Mention (tagging) entity for posts/comments. Captures normalized reference to a mention of a member within a post. Maintains 3NF—each mention is a single entry relating post and mentioned member, supporting notification infrastructure. Unique for (post, mentioned member) pairs.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the model instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_post_id
foreignFields.description: Post's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}. Points to the location where the mention occurred.

foreignFields.name: mentioned_member_id
foreignFields.description: Mentioned user's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. The user referenced in the post/comment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this mention was created, used for notification ordering.

models.name: discussionboard_notifications
models.description:
Discussion Board Notification - This implements the notification delivery and alerting requirement from the requirements documents (particularly 03_discussionboard_features_and_functional_specifications.md, section 7 Notifications and Alerts; see also user journeys and business rules). 

Business explanation: Stores detailed notifications generated by the system—such as mentions, replies, moderator actions, and administrative announcements—to be delivered to specific users. Ensures users are promptly informed of activity requiring their attention. Maintains full 3NF compliance: notification text, type, and linkage to recipient are atomic and non-redundant. For example, when a user is mentioned in a comment, a notification is created here detailing the context and recipient. 

Key relationships: References discussionboard_members as notification recipient; may also reference other entities (e.g., post/thread) as optional context if needed (not included here, but ID pattern allows for future extension). 
Special behaviors: Soft deletion via nullable deleted_at; status/opened flag; delivery details and related timestamps for auditability and analytics; all notifications are individualized and immutable after creation. Audit trails of delivery status handled within this model.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each notification record. Ensures entity uniqueness and supports distributed environments. Required for all entities for tracking and referencing.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Recipient's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Indicates which member this notification is intended for. Enables delivery targeting and audit trail. Required for all notifications.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Notification type - Implements requirement for distinguishing system, user, moderation, and announcement notifications. Possible values: 'mention', 'reply', 'moderator_action', 'announcement', etc. Ensures clear categorization for UI badge and analytics. Example: When a thread is locked, moderators receive a 'moderator_action' type notification. Atomic and fully normalized.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Notification title or brief summary - Implements clear communication of subject as required by UX guidelines. Summarizes notification content in a single line for user display. Example: 'You were mentioned in a post.' Fully normalized.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full textual content of the notification - Implements rich, readable notification context as required by the user journey and business rules. Contains detailed context such as source thread or action taken. Example: 'Your post in "2025 Elections Economy" was edited by a moderator.'

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: Optional URI to direct recipient to the notification context. Supports quick navigation to relevant thread, post, or profile. Implements UX quick-access requirement. Example: '/thread/abc123/post/xyz456'.

plainFields.name: opened
plainFields.description: Whether the notification has been opened/read by the recipient - Implements user status tracking for badge counts & UX feedback. Example: New notifications are false; becomes true when user visits notification center or clicks link. Fully normalized with no redundant status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Notification creation timestamp. Implements requirement to log when notifications are generated, for both UX ordering and audit trails. Non-nullable for history and analytics purposes.

plainFields.name: opened_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the notification was opened/read. Enables precise auditing and user interaction analytics. Nullable for unopened notifications. Ensures atomic status-tracking in 3NF structure.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Implements compliance with audit and retention policies. Marks notification as deleted (hidden from end-user), but retention for admin/audit. Nullable; only set on soft delete.

models.name: discussionboard_alerts
models.description:
Discussion Board Alert - Implements the alerts/urgent notifications requirement from the requirements analysis (03_discussionboard_features_and_functional_specifications.md, section 7; plus cross-reference with moderation & audit policies). 

Business explanation: This table stores urgent, high-visibility system or policy alerts targeted at users, typically for critical events (e.g., suspension warnings, urgent moderation outcomes, system-wide updates). Alerts are designed to demand prominent attention in user UI compared to routine notifications. Fully 3NF: each alert is atomic, unrelated fields and entity-specific details are externalized, audit events logged separately. For example, if a member is suspended, an alert is generated and displayed in a prominent banner.

Key relationships: References discussionboard_members for alert recipient.
Special behaviors: Alerts are prioritized for UI, include severity/type, full body, status, and are audited with timestamps. Could link to moderation/incident report context (future extension).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this alert, ensuring system-wide traceability and immutability.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Recipient's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Indicates which member this alert is for. Delivers alerts to the user's alert center or dashboard. Mandatory foreign key reference.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Alert type/category - Implements requirement to indicate nature and urgency (e.g., 'suspension_warning', 'policy_update', 'system_notice', 'important_announcement'). Used in UI sorting/filtering and analytics. Atomic and normalized.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the alert (e.g., 'critical', 'warning', 'info'). Implements requirement to differentiate UI treatment. Example: 'critical' triggers red banner; 'info' is less intrusive. Fully normalized, non-redundant.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Short alert headline - Implements prominent display and user clarity on subject. Example: 'Suspension Warning'. Used for attention-grabbing summaries in alerts center. Normalized for search/display.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full body of the alert - Implements detailed communication requirement for urgent incidents. Contains full explanation, relevant context, and actionable guidance. Example: 'Your account is suspended for policy violation XYZ.' Atomic, normalized.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Alert is currently active and should be shown to user. Implements business rule for auto-dismissing resolved alerts, supports front-end badge logic, and analytics. Example: Suspension alert is_active until reinstated. Non-redundant, atomic trimmed down to status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the alert was generated. Supports audit and time-sequencing in UI. Fully normalized, required for analytics. Non-nullable.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: When the alert was marked as resolved/dismissed by system or recipient. Implements ability to archive past high-severity alerts, supports analytics on resolution speed. Nullable for active/unresolved alerts only. 3NF compliant.

models.name: discussionboard_search_histories
models.description: User-initiated search activity log - This implements the history and analytics requirements from the requirements analysis (Features and Functional Specifications: Section 5 - Search, Filtering, and Discovery). Records each search operation performed by a user, tied to their account if available or anonymized if performed by a guest, along with search keywords, filter usage, and timestamp. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic search operation data. For example, a member searching for 'budget deficit' will trigger an entry recording their member ID, search query, selected filters, and time of search. Key relationships: Optionally references member actor from already existing actors table discussionboard_members via foreign key. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion possible, sensitive to privacy controls; no computed result counts included.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Globally unique identifier for each search history record.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Related member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} if search is performed by authenticated member. Null if guest or unauthenticated.

plainFields.name: search_query
plainFields.description: Search text entered by user - Implements the requirement for recording used keywords. Stores the exact query string submitted.

plainFields.name: used_filters
plainFields.description: Serialized list of filter identifiers applied during search. Implements analytics and recall requirements. For example: 'tag:macroeconomics,section:current_events'.

plainFields.name: executed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the search was performed. Implements chronology and audit trail requirements.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft-deletion timestamp, null if active. Supports log cleanup, rights to be forgotten, and privacy controls.

models.name: discussionboard_tagged_threads
models.description: Thread-tag link (junction table) - Implements associating threads with tags for flexible discovery and search. This is a junction table supporting a M:N relationship between discussionboard_threads and discussionboard_thread_tags. Fully normalized, containing only atomic foreign keys and the created_at timestamp. For instance, if a thread is tagged with 'fiscal policy' and 'budget', there will be two entries (one per tag) in this table. Key relationships: Links a thread from discussionboard_threads and a tag from discussionboard_thread_tags. Special behaviors: Enforces uniqueness on (thread, tag) pair, supports fast lookup for search and filtering, includes creation timestamp for audit trail.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each thread-tag relationship instance.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_id
foreignFields.description: Targeted thread's {@link discussionboard_threads.id}. Enables linking to a thread entity.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_thread_tag_id
foreignFields.description: Associated tag's {@link discussionboard_thread_tags.id}. Enables M:N association.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of tag assignment. Implements auditability and order-by-recent requirement.

models.name: discussionboard_thread_tags
models.description: Discussion thread tag library - Implements tagging, search, and organization requirements, allowing tag-based topic discovery and moderation. This table stores a catalog of available tags that can be assigned to threads, such as 'economy', 'election', or 'policy'. Maintains 3NF by not including aggregate info, only atomic tag data. For example, site admin creates/tag 'fiscal_policy', which members can assign to threads. Key relationships: Referenced by tagged-thread junction table. Uniqueness by code. Special behaviors: Tag codes are unique, names are searchable, can be marked as moderated/restricted via flags.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique ID for each tag definition.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Canonical tag code. Implements uniqueness and fast search requirement. Lower-case alphanumeric/underscore.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Tag display name, e.g. 'Fiscal Policy'. User-friendly labeling.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Explanation or usage guideline for this tag. Fulfills moderation/discussion guideline mapping. Nullable if not present.

plainFields.name: is_restricted
plainFields.description: Tag moderation flag. If true, only moderators/admins can assign tag. Implements requirements for moderated tags.

plainFields.name: is_hidden
plainFields.description: Soft deprecation flag. If true, users should not see/assign this tag except admin.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of tag creation. Implements audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated. Allows admin track of edits to tags.

models.name: discussionboard_filters
models.description: Saved search/filter configuration - Implements the 'filters' and 'recall/discovery tools', for example, members saving useful filter sets for fast access or sharing. Records configurations for reusable search or discovery filters, which can be user-specific (member) or system-wide. Strictly 3NF: only atomic filter info. For example, a member can save a filter called 'Recent Elections' for all threads with tag 'elections' in 'current events' section, stored as a JSON or string formula. Key relationships: References member for user-specific filters via foreign key. System-wide filters are marked by null member id. Special behaviors: Unique name per user, supports public/private visibility, allows deletion (soft).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. ID for each filter definition.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Filter owner's {@link discussionboard_members.id} if user-specific. Null if shared/system-wide.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Name for this filter as seen by user. Unique per owner (enforced by index). Atomic string. For example: 'Recent Macroeconomics'.

plainFields.name: definition
plainFields.description: Serialized filter definition (could be a query language or JSON-based formula). For example: '{tags: ["elections"], section: "current_events"}'.

plainFields.name: is_public
plainFields.description: Visibility setting. True if filter is shared or system-wide, false if private to member.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of filter creation. For filtering, order-by, and audit.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated. For management and recall tools.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion (null if active). For removal and right-to-be-forgotten policies.

models.name: discussionboard_business_rules
models.description:
Business Rule Definition - This implements the requirement for system-wide governance and operational rules, mapped from section 5.1 of the requirements analysis (Business Rules and Policies). 

Defines a single rule with versioning and enforcement notes, allowing traceability of policy enforcement. Maintains 3NF by storing only atomic rule data, with version history tracked elsewhere. For example, 'No hate speech' or 'Maximum post length'.

Key relationships: May be referenced by platform policy and audit log entities. 
Special behaviors: Immutable after approval except via re-versioning.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each business rule record.

plainFields.name: rule_code
plainFields.description: Machine-friendly rule code - Implements unique policy identification as a short string (e.g., 'NO_HATE_SPEECH'). Facilitates referencing and linking, enforcing uniqueness per rule.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Rule short title - The human-readable name for the rule, for display and audit references. Ensures normalization by storing only the atomic rule label. Used in rule listings and selection forms.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Rule full description - The verbose requirements, restrictions, and definitions for this rule. Maintains normalization by excluding enforcement history or modification logs; only static rule details. Used for admin summaries and user display.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Rule activation flag - Determines if this business rule is currently in effect. Implements EARS specifications for system behavioral toggling; referenced when evaluating enforcement eligibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of rule entry creation. Used for audit and historical reference; never updated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last rule information update (not enforcement event). Tracked only for rule text changes, not enforcement or violation logging.

models.name: discussionboard_platform_policies
models.description:
Platform Policy Statement - Implements explicit documentation and versioning of the platform's rules and policies, based on requirements in the Business Rules and Policies document (section 1 and 3).

Captures high-level policy texts and their publication states, ensuring compliance with audit and transparency values. Maintains 3NF by not embedding related actions, incidents, or appeals.

Usage example: Published privacy policy, content moderation policy, or terms of service, referenced in user interfaces and admin dashboards.

Key relationships: May be linked in notifications or user onboarding flows.
Special behaviors: Replaces previous versions on update; policy text is immutable once published.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each platform policy document.

plainFields.name: policy_code
plainFields.description: Unique policy code - Implements compliance requirement for distinct identification (e.g., 'PRIVACY', 'MODERATION'). Used for referencing and policy change tracking. Enforces uniqueness per active policy.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Policy title - Human-readable title for display and search. Maintains normalization by excluding policy text or status.

plainFields.name: policy_text
plainFields.description: Policy content - The full published text of the policy, supporting platform communication transparency and legal reference. For user agreement and admin review screens.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Policy activation flag - Indicates if this version of the policy is currently in force. Supports rollback on major rule changes.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Publication timestamp - The datetime this policy was rendered active. Used in compliance audits; immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for this policy entry. Tracks administrative changes only, not user or enforcement logs. Required for policy update audit trails.

models.name: discussionboard_audit_logs
models.description:
System Audit Log Entry - Implements the audit trail requirements for sensitive operations, as described in the Security Requirements and Data Retention sections.

Captures each critical action for traceability, legal compliance, and operational review. Maintains 3NF by linking only to atomic action data with foreign keys for originators if implemented in other schemas.

Usage: Whenever a mod/admin changes a rule, enforces a suspension, or alters system access. Allows search by actor, action type, or time window.

Key relationships: May point to actors by actor_id if available.
Special behaviors: Entries are strictly append-only; never updated or deleted except by court order.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each audit log entry.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Action type code - Implements requirement for specific action tracking (e.g., 'RULE_EDIT', 'SUSPENSION_APPLY'). Supports compliance reporting without embedding further context.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the action event taken, for compliance traceability. Maintains normalization by storing only the fact of the action, not duplicating target entity data.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the actor (admin/moderator/member) who performed the action. May reference discussionboard_admins, discussionboard_moderators, or discussionboard_members in Actors schema for referential consistency. Nullable to allow system actions.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the primary entity affected (user, post, policy, etc.). Usage depends on action type. May reference models in other schemas or be null for system-wide actions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of audit log creation. Recorded at the moment of action; immutable.

models.name: discussionboard_incident_reports
models.description:
Incident Report Entity - Implements the incident reporting and escalation workflows from Business Rules and Policies section 4.

Logs reports of rule/policy violations, capturing status, reporting party, action taken (if any), and timestamps. Maintains strict normalization by avoiding embedding of user or policy details; only links by code or ID where necessary. 
Usage example: A member or moderator submits a report of a suspected violation. Tracked through review, escalation, closure.

Key relationships: actor_id and possibly related audit_logs or policies.
Special behaviors: Once closed, cannot be edited; only reopened with admin approval for audits.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Report Identifier.

plainFields.name: incident_code
plainFields.description: Incident code - Unique identifier for each incident (e.g., 'INCIDENT-20240321-001'). Allows search, link to audit logs, and escalation procedures.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Incident status - Workflow indicator (e.g., 'OPEN', 'IN_REVIEW', 'CLOSED', 'ESCALATED'). Implements incident state requirement; supports escalation triggers and closure rules. (Enum recommended in app logic).

plainFields.name: reporter_id
plainFields.description: Actor who submitted the report. UUID value; may reference admins, moderators, or members in Actors schema. Nullable if submitted anonymously.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Incident details - Free text provided by the reporter explaining facts and relevant context. Maintains normalization by not including structured rule data; only the reported statement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Incident report creation timestamp - Used to measure response SLA and escalation timing.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last incident status update (e.g., progress, assignment, closure). Used for internal audit and dashboard tracking.

models.name: discussionboard_appeals
models.description:
Appeal Record - Implements the appeals process for disciplinary or moderation outcomes, as required by the Business Rules and Policies (section 5), including role-based appeal rights and audit trails.

Captures every user-submitted appeal with status and outcome details. Maintains 3NF by recording only atomic data and referencing related incidents or users by ID or code, not duplicating content.

Usage: A sanctioned user (e.g., after a suspension or ban recorded elsewhere) appeals a decision; each appeal is logged with outcome and timestamps.

Key relationships: reporter_id, possibly related incident report or moderation action (cross-schema). 
Special behaviors: Once closed, appeals are immutable; status may affect complaint metrics.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique appeal record identifier.

plainFields.name: appeal_code
plainFields.description: Unique appeal code (e.g., 'APPEAL-20240321-205'). Ensures tracking and cross-referencing with incidents and audit logs.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Appeal status workflow value (e.g., 'PENDING', 'REVIEWING', 'UPHELD', 'REJECTED'). Enables SLA and dashboard reporting; suggested as an Enum in app logic. Maintains normalization by not storing duplicate status details.

plainFields.name: appellant_id
plainFields.description: UUID of user who filed the appeal (may be admin, moderator, or member). Nullable for anonymous, though unusual. Cross-references the Actors models for full details.

plainFields.name: incident_id
plainFields.description: If linked to an incident report, holds the corresponding report's ID for audit and workflow consistency. Nullable for general appeals not tied to a specific incident.

plainFields.name: outcome
plainFields.description: Outcome memo - Short description of the appeal's result once closed (e.g., 'Ban upheld', 'Suspension reversed'). Maintains normalization by storing only atomic outcome description, not related evidence or reasoning.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Appeal submission timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last appeal update timestamp (e.g., outcome decided, status changed).

models.name: discussionboard_categories
models.description: Discussion board categories - Implements categorization as specified in the requirements analysis section regarding navigability, content organization, and moderation targeting. This model supports organized user experience and functional requirements for thread placement, filtering, and role-based content management. Maintains 3NF by keeping category metadata atomic, without duplicating section or configuration data. For example, a member starts a thread under the 'Economics' category, which is mapped here for retrieval. Key relationships: references to discussionboard_sections (for section grouping) and possible linkage to threads (managed in another component). Special behaviors: categories can be disabled or reordered without affecting thread data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each category, supporting distributed system architecture and audit trailing.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_section_id
foreignFields.description: Parent section's {@link discussionboard_sections.id} - Implements hierarchical grouping as per business requirements, enabling categories to be nested within sections for enhanced organization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name - Implements the display and search requirement for category labeling. Ensures normalization by isolating the label as atomic data. For example, 'Politics', 'Economics', 'International' etc.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Category description - Provides contextual information to users and moderators. Maintains normalization by keeping explanations independent of other data. For instance, 'High-level discussions of macroeconomic issues.'

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Category display order - Controls sequence in UI navigation and listings. Maintains 3NF as it's not derived or duplicated from any other data. For example, '1' = top position on board.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Is category enabled - Implements business rule for soft-hiding or disabling a category without deleting its record. Used in admin flows to turn categories on/off. For example, admins can disable a category temporarily during moderation.

models.name: discussionboard_sections
models.description: Discussion board sections - Implements section-level grouping as per requirements covering board segmentation, navigation, and high-level access control. This entity solves the business need for upper-level organization beneath which categories (and subsequently threads) are grouped, supporting both frontend navigation and backend moderation targeting. Fully 3NF: atomic section label, description, and configuration linkage. For example, a section named 'Global Politics' groups multiple categories. Key relationships: can be referenced by categories and linked to board-wide configuration. Special behaviors: sections can be archived, reordered, or locked for content submission by toggling their enabled state.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each section, supporting scalable, distributed storage and system traceability.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Configuration link {@link discussionboard_configurations.id} - Associates the section with platform configuration for access control or behavior settings as per business policy.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section name - Implements navigation and search requirements for board-level organization. Normalized as atomic data. For example, 'Domestic Affairs', 'International Relations'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Section description - Context for users about the topical intent or rules. Fully normalized; avoids data redundancy. For instance, 'Contains threads related to domestic economic policy.'

plainFields.name: order
plainFields.description: Section display order - Determines appearance in navigation and configuration panels. For example, order '0' = top section. 3NF: not dependent on non-key fields.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Is section enabled - Controls visibility and posting capability for the section. Provides admin tools for platform segmentation as required by business rules.

models.name: discussionboard_configurations
models.description: Discussion board configurations - Implements board-wide or section-specific settings, as required by platform policy and business rules for extensibility, permissions, and behavior customization. This model addresses operational flexibility: toggling feature flags, adjusting settings without schema changes, and supporting future platform growth. Maintains strict normalization: each configuration record atomic. For example, holding JSON settings for poll behaviors, default moderation options, or feature enablement. Key relationships: referenced by discussionboard_sections and possibly others in the future. Special behaviors: changes are audit-logged elsewhere; configurations are never deleted outright—only updated or replaced.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration, supporting distributed storage and reliable referencing by other entities.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Configuration name/key - Used for identification in admin tools and code. Normalized primary config label. Example: 'default_section_policy', 'poll_settings'.

plainFields.name: settings_json
plainFields.description: Serialized configuration JSON - Stores all behavioral settings as a JSON string. Normalized: each config in its own row. For example, '{"allow_polls": true, "max_poll_options": 10}'

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable descriptive text about the configuration's purpose. Maintains normalization. For instance, 'Settings controlling default behaviors for domestic threads.'

models.name: discussionboard_admins
models.description:
Admin Role Model - This implements the administrative user role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents site administrators who have full access for platform management, policy enforcement, user control, and official dispute handling. Maintains 3NF normalization by only holding role-specific identity, inheriting account details via shared foreign key references in actual system (e.g., via member or user account tables in other domains). For example, admins may be mapped to existing accounts for login. 

Key relationships: Not directly referencing other components to avoid duplication, but will use external user/member tables for ID in full implementation. 
Special behaviors: Only users elevated to this table have admin permissions; removal here revokes all admin rights.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique admin role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Implements the auditability requirement. Records when the admin privilege was granted. Ensures temporal traceability for permission changes, supporting snapshot patterns by explicitly separating the assignment history. For example, when new admins are added, this field logs the event.

models.name: discussionboard_moderators
models.description:
Moderator Role Model - This implements the moderator role specification from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents users with moderation powers: content review, temporary suspensions, and community management, without full admin rights. 3NF compliance is achieved by separating moderator role assignments from general user/member identity, with actual references made to external user/member accounts for linkage. 

Key relationships: In a full system, would reference members/users for role mapping. 
Special behaviors: Inclusion grants moderation rights; records are auditable for community trust and escalation protocols.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique moderator role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Tracks when the moderator privilege was activated. Supports audit trails and historical analysis of role distribution and trust elevation. For example, elevated by senior admins or via governance process.

models.name: discussionboard_members
models.description:
Member Role Model - Implements core registered user account role as specified in '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents all authenticated users authorized to create content, interact, and participate in member-only features. Complies with 3NF by storing only role/enrollment information; user profile, security, and credentials exist in separate tables/domains. For example, email/username/password managed elsewhere but ID assigned here upon registration completion.

Key relationships: Mapped to outer user or authentication entity in wider system. 
Special behaviors: Granting/removing a row in this table assigns permission to create threads, participate in polls, etc.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique member role identifier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Role assignment timestamp - Logged at registration or membership upgrade. Used for eligibility/rule tracking and supports audit trails. For example, new signups receive this timestamp.

models.name: discussionboard_guests
models.description:
Guest Role Model - Implements the guest browsing entity from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md'. 

Represents unauthenticated and optionally semi-tracked users who may browse public content but not post/interact. Maintains 3NF as a distinct normalized table to assign and trace guest viewing sessions, apply access controls, and support future conversion (upgrade to member). For example, may store guest session or visitor tokens mapped to analytics.

Key relationships: May relate to external analytics/logs for guest tracking in broader system. 
Special behaviors: Deleting a guest here does not affect any member/admin records, ensuring normalization between roles.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique guest identifier, e.g., guest session or pseudonymous token.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Guest session/browsing assignment timestamp - Set when a guest session is first tracked or created. Used for analysis, conversion tracking to members, and policy enforcement (e.g., access window).

models.name: discussionboard_auth_sessions
models.description:
Authentication Session Model - Implements the authentication and session tracking requirement from '02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_authentication.md' and ties policies in '05_discussionboard_business_rules_and_policies.md' (account locking, session expiry, etc.). 

Tracks active user/member sessions for login management, enforcing security policies, session timeouts, and role mapping. Complies with 3NF by separating session management from user identity, allowing independent lifecycle. For example, on login, a new row is created; on logout or expiry, row is ended.

Key relationships: Would reference user/member/role tables for session ownership in a full system.
Special behaviors: Supports device/session concurrency policies, auditing of all critical actions (policy: audit trail for edits, deletions, moderation decisions).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique session identifier.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Role type associated with the session. Implements session role typing for permission checks (e.g., 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', 'guest'). Ensures normalization by separating session against role tables. For example: 'member' session tracks a logged in member, 'guest' for unauthenticated visitor.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Associated actor id (admin/member/moderator/guest). Implements role linking for session ownership. Ensures normalization so that user/role are tracked externally, this is a foreign key reference in broader system. For example, points to the 'id' of the corresponding role table depending on actor_type.

plainFields.name: issued_at
plainFields.description: Session start timestamp. Implements session record creation for login audit trails. For example, set when user completes login.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp - Used to implement session expiry, security policy on inactivity, or explicit logout. For example, calculated by security policy or upon logout event.

plainFields.name: last_activity_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last activity on this session. Implements last-used tracking for security checks (token expiration, forced logout). For example, updated on each page load or action.

plainFields.name: revoked_at
plainFields.description: Time at which session was revoked, if applicable. Implements security and forced logout. For example, set if session is invalidated by admin or system.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address recorded when session was initiated. Provides security auditing for login source and supports fraud monitoring. For example, '192.168.1.1'.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string recorded on session establishment. Implements browser/device tracking policy for audit and security. For example, 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10...)'.

models.name: discussionboard_threads
models.description:
Thread Root Entity - This implements the 'thread management and creation' requirement from the features and user journeys documentation. Each instance represents an individual discussion thread (topic) started by a member, with links to category/section and root post. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating main thread data (title, status, author/member, section/category) from posts, histories, and related engagement. For example, a new thread '2025 Elections Discussion' would have one record here and many related post/comment records elsewhere. 
Key relationships: Links to author member, category, and root post via foreign keys. Special behaviors: Soft-deletion (archived flag), per-thread lock/pin status for moderation/admins.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique thread identifier.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Thread author's {@link discussionboard_members.id}. Refers to the member who created the thread.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_category_id
foreignFields.description: Thread's assigned {@link discussionboard_categories.id}. Refers to the topic/category under which this thread is created.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Thread title - Implements the required summary/title as per requirements document. Atomic, and always present. For example: '2025 Economic Outlook'.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Thread status - Active, archived, locked. Implements moderation control requirement. For example: 'active', 'locked', 'archived'.

plainFields.name: is_pinned
plainFields.description: Pinned flag - Whether this thread is pinned at the top. Implements thread management feature for moderators/admins. true if pinned by moderation.

plainFields.name: is_locked
plainFields.description: Locked flag - Whether this thread is locked. Implements moderation tool for controlling participation. true if thread no longer accepts replies.

plainFields.name: archived
plainFields.description: Soft delete/archive flag. If true, thread is hidden from public but data is retained for admins/audit. Implements audit/compliance rules.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Thread creation timestamp. For audit/logging as per business rules.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Thread last updated timestamp. Updated on edits or moderation events. Required for audit trail and UX.

models.name: discussionboard_posts
models.description: Thread Post Entity - Implements the 'thread and comment posting', 'reply', and 'content moderation/reporting' features. Each represents an individual post or comment in a thread, with parent-child relation for comments (nested structure).
